lede: Latent size 8 wins the search, and Fashion-MNIST comes out cleaner than digits.
title: Digits against Fashion-MNIST
question: With the same VAE, how do reconstruction, likelihood, and samples from the prior differ on the two datasets?
process: The encoder does not return a single code. It returns the mean and the log-variance of a diagonal Gaussian q(z|x). A sample is drawn so that a gradient still passes through it:

The decoder maps that sample back to pixels. The loss adds reconstruction error to a closed-form KL divergence against N(0, I). Squared error is summed over pixels, the KL is summed over latent axes, and both terms are averaged over the batch:
In this comparison β is fixed at 1. A reconstruction decodes the posterior mean. A sample decodes a draw from N(0, I), with the encoder left out.

Four Optuna trials scored latent sizes 2, 8, 16, and 32, with validation losses 118.1, 95.9, 101.4, and 107.4. Latent size 8 was kept. On a slice of 1,000 images per class, Fashion-MNIST reaches test MSE 0.075 and ELBO −71.1. Digits reach test MSE 0.085 and ELBO −82.2.

opening.summary: Latent size 8 has the lowest validation loss of the four trials, and both datasets were scored with that checkpoint.
opening.hover: Compare the two datasets, then the search over latent size.

charts.title: Test scores for the same model

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: On digits, test MSE is 0.0852, KL is 15.41, and ELBO is −82.21. Domain KID is 3.1052. Samples from the prior still look like digits, but a blurry decoder drops thin strokes first. The spatial KID says those samples sit farther from the test set than the Fashion-MNIST samples do.
marks.frameCaption: Digit samples from the prior. Thick strokes, and many classes.

marks.summary: On Fashion-MNIST, test MSE is 0.0749, KL is 12.34, and ELBO is −71.09. Domain KID is 0.2043. Shirts, shoes, trousers, and bags still read as those objects when the decoder is soft, because the silhouette is wide. The same blur hurts a one-pixel stroke much more.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion-MNIST samples from the prior. Shirts, trousers, shoes, and bags.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Latent size 2 is the worst of the four finished trials, with validation loss 118.06. Every other setting was held fixed: hidden size 256, dropout 0.1, learning rate 0.001, weight decay 1e-6, and batch size 128. The code is too small for the ELBO on this slice.

Latent size 8 is marked because it has the minimum validation loss, 95.93, and Optuna minimizes that loss. The saved hyperparameters record this trial. Both the digit and Fashion-MNIST checkpoints use it. Latent size 16 scores 101.37 and latent size 32 scores 107.42, so a wider code made this short search worse.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: Latent size 16 scores a validation loss of 101.37, above latent size 8. Four epochs on this slice is a short fit, and the extra coordinates are not yet paying for themselves in the ELBO.

marks.answers: How could the results be improved?
marks.summary: Latent size 32 scores 107.42, the second-worst trial. A longer training run on the full 60,000 images is the next measurement. The f-VAE below does use latent size 32 on the full split, so it is a different experiment.

reflection.worked: Latent size 8 wins the four-trial search, at validation loss 95.9. On the scored slice, Fashion-MNIST beats digits on MSE, ELBO, KL, and KID, and both sample grids are readable. The RealNVP inverses are not.
reflection.unexpected: Latent sizes 16 and 32 score worse than 8 on this short search, at 101.4 and 107.4. Digit samples look readable and still lose on domain KID, 3.11 against 0.20.
reflection.why: Both scored runs use 1,000 images per class, and the per-epoch record is the loss figure rather than a numeric series. A reasonable reading is that the same blur removes a one-pixel stroke and leaves a shirt, which is why KID separates the datasets more sharply than MSE.
reflection.improve: Retrain both models on the full split of 60,000 images, and write the per-epoch ELBO next to the final table. This slice and the full-split f-VAE are different experiments, and should not be compared as if they were the same run.
